title: Lisa Su Just Delivered Fantastic News for AMD Investors
detail:
Lisa Su Just Delivered Fantastic News for AMD Investors
Keithen Drury, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 2:46 PM MST 5 min read
AMD
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) CEO Lisa Su has a great track record. She resurrected the company from irrelevance and is now leading it into the age of AI. The stock has had a rough few weeks, as it reached an all-time high in early October, then proceeded to sell off by about 25%. However, it got a bit of a bounce after it delivered its latest earnings report on Nov. 3, and that's all thanks to some items that Su has positioned AMD to take advantage of, as well as some forward-looking comments she gave.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But does that make AMD a buy right now? Let's take a look.

AMD CEO Lisa Su. Image source: Advanced Micro Devices.
AMD's Q3 was impressive

AMD makes an array of types of computing chips. Whether you're talking about central processing units (CPUs) for personal computers or GPUs for gaming or data centers, AMD is in those markets. Compared to rival Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), AMD is far more diversified in terms of its end markets, which has hurt it given how much of the tech sector's recent growth has been coming from data centers. However, AMD has taken steps to improve its position in that market, and is now seeing impressive data center growth.

In Q3, revenue in that segment was up 97% year over year to $8.5 billion. Still, that was a deceleration from the 107% year-over-year growth it experienced during Q2. Normally, a result like that might have prompted a negative stock reaction, but Su stepped in to save the day on the earnings call. She noted that AMD expects server revenue to double year over year in 2027, and reported that AI-related growth was accelerating compared to where management thought it would be last quarter. That's huge news for investors, but what does it mean for the rest of AMD's business?

While its data center business provides the majority of its revenue now, AMD's other segments still play large roles. However, they were quite weak. Revenues from its client and gaming division (consumer hardware) were down 8% year over year. Its embedded division saw revenue rise 29% year over year, but it only generated $1.1 billion in revenue, versus client and gaming's $3.7 billion and data centers' $8.5 billion. The 45% companywide growth rate is impressive, but the lackluster results from the consumer division are still a drag on that figure.

The problem is, AMD is being valued like it's only a data center investment.

Nvidia plunged 18% in five sessions, erasing roughly $913 billion, as a probe into Jensen Huang and China chip-transfer reports spooked investors.

Most analysts keep Buy ratings with targets implying over 80% upside, though Baird downgraded and slashed its target from $500 to $200.

AMD gained and Broadcom held flat during the selloff, so the damage was Nvidia-specific, and November 17 earnings become the first real test.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) trades at $177.22, and Wall Street's average price target is $325.78. At that price, the target means 83.83% upside.

Wikimedia Commons

Most of that gap opened over five sessions. By our calculation, the stock fell 18.29% from a $206.69 close. Based on Tuesday's $4.08 trillion market value and 24.15 billion shares, we estimate about $913 billion of value was erased.

Tuesday's $168.89 close was the stock's lowest since a $165.17 finish in late March. A gap this wide usually signals that analysts and the market disagree about something basic. Here, the disagreement is over governance and China exposure, even as NVIDIA says demand for its chips still outpaces supply.

Earnings come out November 17 after the close. That report will be the first hard test of whether the targets or the stock price is closer to right.

How Five Days Beat DeepSeek and Most of 2022

This was NVIDIA's worst five-session stretch since the one that ended September 1, 2022. In that stretch, the split-adjusted stock fell 22.2%, from $17.91 to $13.94. A window that ended in April 2022 was also worse, with a 19.89% drop, so "since 2022" means since that September.

The DeepSeek comparison sets five days against five days. NVIDIA lost 16.97% in a single January 2025 session, falling from $142.62 to $118.42. Its worst five sessions around that shock cost 15.89%.

This week's slide was also bigger than the 17.22% drop over the five sessions that ended in September 2024. No single day came close to the DeepSeek session. The worst was a 9.26% fall to $181.60.

We just published a list of the Analysts Just Slashed Their Price Targets on These 10 Stocks and Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) ranked 8th on this list.

Wall Street had its worst day in 19 months last Thursday, with chip stocks leading the selloff. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315.00, its biggest one-day drop since the April 2025 tariff announcement. The S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, erasing about $3 trillion in market value and marking its worst day since that same tariff crash. The Dow lost 3.44%.

The Nasdaq is now in a correction, more than 10% below the record close it set last month. Volume was heavy: 26.9 billion shares changed hands, against a 20-session average of 17.7 billion.

10 Stocks Analysts Are Upgrading Right Now
Fear of Tighter AI Rules Hit Chip Stocks

The trigger was politics. Investors worried about tighter AI regulation after Democrats won control of Congress, including in states where opposition to new data centers has been growing. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index fell more than 12% in one session, its worst day since March 2020. Candidates in both parties had campaigned against AI data centers, Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre reported.

Melissa Brown, global head of investment decision research at SimCorp, said some newly elected members of Congress and governors want to slow the pace of AI infrastructure development, and that any slowdown would raise concerns. We covered the group's earlier pullback in our list of oversold AI stocks that Wall Street analysts saw 50%+ upside in, published before the selloff.

A Partial Rebound, With Rate Hikes Still in View

Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, called Thursday "the capitulation phase for the data center capex beneficiary stocks" and said the size of the moves looked excessive. Chip stocks did bounce on Friday: the semiconductor index rose 4.2% and the Nasdaq gained 1.1% to 24,579.43, and the S&P 500 rose 0.32% to 7,376.86, while the Dow slipped 0.46% to 51,285.73. But the Nasdaq still posted its fourth straight weekly decline, down 3.4% for the week, while the S&P 500 fell 2.7%, its worst week since June, and the Dow fell 0.9%.

Readers weighing how far the technology sector has fallen can also look at our roundup of technology stocks trading near 52-week lows that analysts favor. Through Thursday's close, the S&P 500 was still up 7.4% for 2026 and the Nasdaq up 4.6%. Friday's jobs report showed employers added 165,000 jobs in October, against 59,000 expected, and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%. Traders expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates next month, following a hike in September.

Why Advanced Micro Devices Stock Popped Today

CRWV
AMD
NVDA

Trading disclosure

A strong earnings report from AI cloud provider CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) Tuesday night is helping lift semiconductor stocks of all shapes and sizes, amid a positive outlook for future sales to AI data centers. That's not the only reason, though, that shares of Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) are up 7.9% through 12:20 p.m. ET today.

Turns out, there's even more good news for AMD!

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

CoreWeave Q3 earnings report

CoreWeave "beat earnings" in its Q3 report last night, losing less money ($1.27 per share) than feared, and collecting more revenue ($3.66 billion) than hoped. That company further raised its guidance for full-year 2026 revenue to a range of from $13.0 billion to $13.3 billion, with better-than-forecast adjusted operating income guidance -- and promised to spend anywhere from $37 billion to $39 billion on capital investment, which was also more than expected.

This is the part most relevant to AMD stock. The more money CoreWeave spends on "capital investment," the more it will spend on AMD CPU chips for its data centers.

AMD is also benefiting from a UBS report out today, which notes that server CPU shipments jumped 31% year over year in Q3. And AMD is holding steady on its CPU market share -- about 28.4% according to UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri -- versus a 240-basis-point decline in Intel's (NASDAQ:INTC) CPU market share. Furthermore, Arcuri believes that CPU prices are rising (meaning more profit for AMD).

What's next for AMD

By 2030, the UBS analyst predicts CPU sales could hit $210 billion, and if AMD maintains its market share, that would mean nearly $60 billion in CPU sales alone for AMD. That's 33% more revenue than AMD currently gets from all its product sales.

Although at 110x earnings, AMD stock may not look cheap right now, AMD's future does look bright.

The filing allocates AMD 33,783,783 shares at the $74 midpoint, the third-largest slice behind Google and NVIDIA. Anthropic states it runs workloads across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs and AMD GPUs, which puts AMD inside one of the largest AI compute buyers. Goldman's James Schneider called AMD "very attractive" for growth but less compelling on valuation, per 24/7 Wall St., and warned that catalysts for a sustained chip rally may be limited before year-end.

At about 0.3% of AMD's market value near $888 billion, the check is financially modest. The real payoff would be share of wallet: if Anthropic shifts more training or inference to Instinct GPUs, the stake could look cheap; if not, it reads as paying for a seat at the table. At $524.07, the shares trade 65.7% above GuruFocus's GF Value of $316.19, and GuruFocus labels them "Significantly Overvalued." The next test is whether data center GPU revenue keeps pace with that premium.

Oppenheimer believes Wall Street could climb beyond its previous highs despite renewed inflation concerns and uncertainty surrounding artificial intelligence spending. The investment bank's bullish outlook comes with two semiconductor picks: Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), which analyst Rick Schafer believes offer substantial upside as demand for AI computing and networking infrastructure accelerates.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with AMD.

Is AMD fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

AMD GF Value chart

Oppenheimer chief investment strategist John Stoltzfus argues that resilient economic fundamentals and corporate earnings could support further stock market gains.

His optimism comes after October inflation exceeded expectations, raising questions about future Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions.

For AMD, Schafer recently upgraded shares to Outperform with a $600 price target, implying approximately 16.5% upside from Tuesday's closing price.

The bullish case centers on AMD's expanding AI computing business.

Third-quarter revenue increased 44% to $13.4 billion, while data center sales surged 97% to $8.5 billion.

Schafer expects data center revenue to grow another 135% in 2027, accounting for approximately 85% of total sales.

AMD's expanding partnerships with major cloud providers, including Google, strengthen its position against Nvidia.

Marvell offers another potentially lucrative opportunity.

Schafer maintains an Outperform rating and $425 price target, implying approximately 175% upside.

The optimism reflects Marvell's proposed $115 billion acquisition of optical networking specialist Lumentum, which could create a major supplier of AI data center connectivity technologies.

Marvell's fiscal second-quarter revenue climbed 37% to $2.74 billion, reinforcing its growth momentum.

Investors Takeaway

For AMD, investors should monitor AI accelerator shipments, data center margins and execution against ambitious 2027 growth expectations.

Marvell shareholders face a different catalyst: regulatory and shareholder approval of the Lumentum acquisition, expected to close in the first half of 2028.

Integration costs, potential dilution and the sustainability of networking demand will also matter.

Both stocks remain exposed to hyperscaler capital spending and semiconductor valuations.

Stronger cloud investment and successful product execution could support Oppenheimer's targets, while slowing AI demand or disappointing margins could undermine its bullish outlook.
